title: Adding Lucene-style ?q= query string search for alerts made the Postgres backend build WHERE clauses by str.format()-ing user search terms into SQL.

findings.explanation: The code has been refactored to use parameterized queries with named parameters (e.g., %(_qp_0)s) instead of string interpolation. User input from search queries is now placed into a separate params dictionary and passed as bound parameters to the database. Field names and operators are still string-interpolated, but they come from the parser's token classification (fieldname, field, op attributes) rather than direct user input. The parser validates these tokens against its grammar rules. While field names are interpolated, they are constrained by the parser logic and appear to be from a limited set of known fields. Parameterized query execution with psycopg2's parameter substitution prevents SQL injection of the values.
